H.Selaram vs The Designated Officer on 2 February, 2024 
Author: S.M.Subramaniam
Bench: S.M.Subramaniam
 W.P.No.18
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras
 Dated : 02.02.2024
 Coram
 The Honourable Mr. Justice S.M.Subramaniam
 W.P.No.1844 of 2021
 H.Selaram ... Pet
 Vs.
 1. The Designated Officer,
 District Food Safety Officer,
 Coimbatore District,
 Coimbatore.
 2. The Food Safety Officer,
 Code No. 559,
 Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration,
 Coimbatore Corporation,
 Coimbatore-641 018 ... Resp
 Prayer :- Writ petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution 
 praying for issuance of a writ of Mandamus, directing the 2nd respon
 to de-seal the petitioners shop situated at D. No. 37 B1 Annai Indir
 Nagar, Chokkampudur Road, Selvapuram, Coimbatore after removal of
 seized article by considering my representations dated 08.10.2020 wi
 the time framed by this Hon'ble Court. 
 For Petitioner : Mr.T.Nixon 
 For Respondents : Mr.V.Veluchamy,
 Additional Government Pleader
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
 1/4

 W.
 Order
H.Selaram vs The Designated Officer on 2 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30023353/
1 The relief sought for in the present writ petition is to direct the 2nd respondent to de-seal the petitioners shop situated at D. No. 37 B1 Annai Indira Nagar, Chokkampudur Road, Selvapuram,
Coimbatore after removal of seized article by considering my representations dated 08.10.2020. 
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the show cause notice issued by the respondent was responded by the petitioner and an inquiry was conducted. The fine amount of Rs.
25,000/- was imposed on the petitioner and the petitioner paid the fine amount. 
3. Thus, the respondents are directed to verify the said facts and if there is no other impediment,
de-seal the premises by following the procedures as contemplated and by imposing necessary conditions, if any. 
Accordingly, the writ petition stands disposed of. However, there shall be no order as to costs.
